name: bench-x86_64
label: bench-host
machine_label: 2x Xeon E5-2673 v4 (2x20 cores, SMT on), bare metal, fixed 2.3 GHz, turbo off, default idle states; rungs of 1 to 28 workers, main thread on its own core

micro.invol_bound_record: frozen from the bare-metal smokes of 2026-11-18 (fix build, atomic_model, 0.2 s windows, no CPU isolation): 18:43:40Z 0-4 per repetition over 60 repetitions (26 x 0, 17 x 1, 10 x 2, 2 x 3, 5 x 4); 18:45:23Z at most 6 (4 threads). The counter is summed over the threads; rule: per thread max(5, 25/s x window), times the threads (5 per thread at 0.2 s, 25 per thread at 1 s)

note: The bench box. CPU sets follow the plan's rung table; the client and origin share the cores outside the worker sets and the main thread's, siblings included; the harness itself gets one core.

u_hi.note: run U at 1,000 per worker held the workers 25-28% busy; the client threads were 31% busy at 14 workers and 39% at 28 workers (14 client workers, 14 CPUs), so the 25% headroom gate bounds 28 workers near 1,900 per worker (about 50% worker busy) unless the client does better than linear; the calibration decides

attempts.result: stopped 2026-11-19 15:55-16:32 CET: 8 of 15 28w legs invalid (6 other tasks on the SUT CPUs 0.053-0.071 against 0.05, 2 client pool overflow); 31 valid, 8 invalid; kept as a failed attempt

cells.rate_note: 3,000 per worker ran the workers at 81% busy with the K = 128 logger (pilot attempt 1: about 706k worker cycles per request against 540k without it) and failed the client gates; 2,200 aims at 60-68% busy; the total is then 15,400, not the other cells' 21,000

pilot.order_note: shapes in this order, arms as listed, no re-run of an invalid leg and no stop after consecutive invalid legs: the deciding 16-connection legs of cells A and D, then the other connection count, then the loopback pair, then the exploratory cell

attempts.result: 2026-11-20 09:00-09:06 UTC: stopped after 6 legs, all invalid on the client gates (4 connections per worker at 14 and 28 workers: pool overflow and pending above the limit; 7 workers at 3,000 with 16 connections: 81% busy, overflow, pending); the run order put those shapes first and the six-invalid-legs rule stopped it before any 16-connection leg of cells A and D; 4 connections per worker cannot hold 1,500 per worker on the client side, so the alternative count is 8

pilot_rule.k_rule: the smallest K with h x K x cycles_per_transfer / own worker cycles per request >= min_share in the cell
pilot_rule.connections_rule: the connection count with the smaller |clean L3 hits per update, own - shared| at the middle K in the cell, provided every leg at that count is valid in the connection cells; else the other count if its legs are valid

dose.listener_note: every dose arm listens on the wildcard address: Envoy then reads each accepted connection's local address into its own object, where a loopback listener gives every connection of every worker the listener's one address object (the address formatter copies its shared pointer once per counter); the client still targets 127.0.0.1; the admin port stays on loopback
dose.hitm_events_note: cycles is user and kernel on one counter (as in hitm_events): with the three memory-load events the list then needs at most four programmable counters even when the fixed cycles counter is taken
dose.flush_note: every dose arm sets this stats flush interval: longer than a leg's Envoy lives (about a minute), under the 300 s the bootstrap accepts, so the main thread's flush does not latch the own arms' counters during the window; base and stats-reject keep the default 5 s
dose.client_duration_note: run U's client runs 25 s for a 3 s lead-in and a 20 s window; the dose legs read tens of thousands of counters over the admin port before the window, which comes out of that slack, so their client runs 30 s; the window is the same 20 s
dose.note: run R1 (dose): K stats-access-logger counters per request, shared by all workers (tag = the listener port) against one set per downstream connection (tag = the client port), on a wildcard listener; slot cells A, B and D (run U's 28w rung) at 1,500 per worker, cell A also at K / 4; cell C (7 workers at 3,000, the dose run's own rung) in the pilot only, exploratory; rates_key holds the pilot's choice as {"counters": K, "connections": connections per worker}, one key per attempt
